clue.text: One seducing US singer reserves a room

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep something held back, so the singer's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Cher, the American pop singer
taken as written
RM is the standard abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: An American pop star books a room, presumably for a romantic rendezvous.
explanation.walkthrough: CH(A RM)ER: the singer's name is split open to hold the article and the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer is a person who attracts and beguiles others, which is what someone seducing does.

clue.text: Cell initially needing permission to divide

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of cell
leave is permission, as in leave to appeal

explanation.surface: A biology picture: a cell must first be allowed before it can split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' simply puts the permission after the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split or sever something, one of the word's two opposite senses.

clue.text: In moat he struggles

indicators.note: something that struggles thrashes about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man is floundering in the water of a castle moat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single short word at the front; it reads as a preposition in the surface but means 'not out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in is present at their house, available to callers rather than out.

clue.text: Swallow good beer going for broke at casino

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
G is the usual abbreviation for good
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A gambler downs a decent pint before staking everything at the tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking the beer, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The martingale is a betting system in which a gambler doubles the stake after every loss, risking ruin.

clue.text: Old magistrate once a Kent player?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a medieval English local official or chief magistrate
second meaning: the actor Christopher ..., who played Clark Kent in the Superman films

explanation.surface: Was some historic local official once a cricketer for the county of Kent?
explanation.walkthrough: Kent suggests the English county cricket team; it is Clark Kent, Superman's alter ego, and the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was an official in medieval England, and Christopher Reeve was the film actor who portrayed Clark Kent.

clue.text: First established position to see bishop exiting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: exiting means leaving, so the abbreviation named goes out of the word

parts.note: behold means see
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church setting: the first secure ground in a diocese once the bishop has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a bishop's diocese, which fits the surface, but it is the verb behold.
explanation.definitionFit: A toehold is a small initial foothold, a first position gained from which to advance.

clue.text: Rapper on stage to milk a reindeer?

parts.note: to tap is to draw off liquid, as from a cask or a tree
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A hip-hop performer onstage attempts to milk a reindeer, a silly picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The rapper is not a hip-hop artist but one who raps the floor with metal-tipped shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap dancer performs on stage by striking the floor rhythmically, so is literally one who raps.

clue.text: See 12
Partial description of Möbius strip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: biased, favouring one party
second meaning: a Möbius strip has a single surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial' looks like 'incomplete' but means biased.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased account favours one party, and a Möbius strip, a twisted loop of paper, has only a single surface.

clue.text: Cobblers perhaps tense up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: tense means stressed, anxious

explanation.surface: Shoemakers, perhaps, get nervous and wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobblers are shoe menders on the surface, but a cobbler is also a baked fruit pudding; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler is a fruit pudding with a scone topping, so cobblers are examples of puddings.

clue.text: Subtract any number from lower number

indicators.note: subtract means take away, so a letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: An arithmetic instruction: take some number away from a smaller one.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early general anaesthetic, a substance that makes a patient numb.

clue.text: Vacancy M&S filled with essentially dippy case?

indicators.note: something filled with stuff has it inside, so the letters named go between the two outer pieces

parts.note: the letter M spelled out as its name

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the central letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of dippy
a tin is a case or container
the letter S spelled out as its name

explanation.surface: A shop window at Marks & Spencer stands empty, filled only with a silly display case.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is not the store: the two letters are written out as their names, EM and ESS, which then hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptiness is the state of being vacant, so it is a synonym for vacancy.

clue.text: Claret consumer in club following Siren and Fury

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece named first in the clue is placed last

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive woman, a siren
ire is fury, anger
a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A wine drinker at a nightclub comes after two dramatic women, a Siren and a Fury from myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is slang for blood. 'following' places the club after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The vampire bat feeds on the blood of animals, and claret is slang for blood.

clue.text: Burning issue

parts.note: surface reading: a pressing, urgent topic of debate
setter's reading: a way out, an issue, used when a building is ablaze

explanation.walkthrough: Issue here means a way out, as in egress, and burning means on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the emergency doorway people leave by when a building is ablaze, an issue in the old sense of outlet.

clue.text: Crazy lunacy having Welshman in Chekhov drama

indicators.note: crazy means deranged, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A mad Russian play in which a Welshman appears, an incongruous casting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welshman is added to the fodder before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Vanya is one of Anton Chekhov's best-known plays, first staged in 1899.

clue.text: This attained so one can get involved with female

definitions.text: This attained so one can get involved with female

indicators.note: involved means entangled, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A sober legal explanation of when a young man may lawfully begin a relationship with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: reaching this milestone lets a person lawfully become involved with a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the legal age at which someone may agree to sexual relations, so once reached one may get involved.

clue.text: Liverpudlian singer in old set rewritten for swing?

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: in places the singer's name inside the reworked letters
something rewritten has been recast, so its letters come out in a different order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
Cilla Black, the singer from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A Merseyside singer revises an old set list to add a swing number.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a Liverpool pop singer and TV presenter of the 1960s onward.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to move back and forth regularly, the motion of a pendulum or swing.

clue.text: Waste initially cleared after a flush

indicators.note: cleared at the start means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
effluent is liquid waste or sewage

explanation.surface: A plumbing scene: waste water clearing away after the toilet is flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the trimmed waste behind the article. Flush is the definition, an adjective meaning well off, not the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having plenty of money, so it is a synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Sophisticated group examine sheep from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from below means read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: to test is to examine
rams are male sheep

explanation.surface: A vet is told to inspect the sheep from underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The smart set are fashionable, sophisticated people, a social clique.

clue.text: Blood group O?

parts.note: surface reading: the blood type O, from medical tests
setter's reading: a group of blood relatives, with the letter O standing for a round shape

explanation.walkthrough: Blood means kin, and the letter O is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one's relatives and close kin, people related by blood, and O is shaped like a ring.

clue.text: Rules of engagement?

parts.note: surface reading: military orders governing when troops may open fire
setter's reading: terms a betrothed couple agree before the wedding

explanation.walkthrough: Engagement is the betrothal, not a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a legal agreement drawn up by an engaged couple, setting out how assets are split if they divorce.

clue.text: Key again right with Jaguar model

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A car owner gets a replacement key for a Jaguar sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: Key looks like a car key, but here it means to type on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To key text is to type it, so keying it again is to type it once more.

clue.text: Mad King Lear loses throne at last in play

indicators.note: mad means deranged, so the remaining letters are jumbled
loses means gives up, so a letter is taken out of the name

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written

indicators.note: at last points at the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of throne

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's deranged King Lear finally loses his crown in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'play' is Shakespeare's tragedy, but as the definition it means fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a prank, and to lark about is to play.

clue.text: Poetry not written on very old language

parts.note: a blank page has nothing written on it
V is the abbreviation for very
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Poems that were never put down on paper, composed in an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is a dated name for the Gaelic languages, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Blank verse is unrhymed iambic pentameter, the form of Shakespeare's and Milton's poetry.

clue.text: Tend to course around Seine's banks

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: a run is a course, as a ski run

indicators.note: a river's banks are its edges, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Seine

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a riverside path along the banks of the Seine in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks of the river fit the surface perfectly, but they just mean its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to look after or care for them, as to tend to them.

clue.text: Parrot in Square Mile on horse with duck

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, the Square Mile
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A menagerie in the City of London: a parrot, a horse and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The Square Mile is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC. 'on' and 'with' simply add pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mindlessly, which is what an echo does.

clue.text: Relax in this undemanding academic post

parts.note: easy means undemanding
a chair is a professorship

explanation.surface: A cushy professorship lets the holder put their feet up.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a comfortable upholstered armchair, the furniture one sinks into to unwind.

clue.text: Article recalled clubs in New York City

indicators.note: in puts the suit abbreviation inside the abbreviation for the American state

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.definitionFit: Nancy is a historic city in Lorraine, north-eastern France.

clue.text: Walked into Peg in the Tube

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube suggests the London Underground; here it is an electronic valve.

clue.text: School test regularly applied pattern

parts.note: an exam is a school test

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of applied
